items.title: Skip Lists Explained: How Coin Flips Make Search Fast
items.author: The Geek Narrator
items.summary:
How can coin flips make a linked list fast? In this visual lightboard lesson, Kaivalya Apte explains skip lists—from express-lane intuition to search, insertion, deletion, and the math behind expected O(log n) performance.

We trace pointer updates, build randomized node heights, and work through the backward-search argument. You'll also see how promotion probability affects memory use and how skip lists compare with balanced trees.

Key takeaway: skip lists give expected O(log n) search, insertion, and deletion, with expected O(n) space for a fixed promotion probability. Individual operations can still take O(n) in the worst case.

Chapters:
00:00 Why sorted linked lists are still slow
01:45 Express lanes: the skip-list intuition
05:36 Coin flips and randomized node heights
07:58 One tower, one node: storing pointers
08:56 The search rule and update array
10:02 Search walkthrough
11:58 Insertion and pointer updates
13:22 Deletion and empty levels
14:27 Why expected O(log n)?
16:49 The backward-search proof
22:09 Expected O(n) space
23:13 Tuning the promotion probability
24:27 Skip lists versus balanced trees
25:49 The four key ideas
